anomalies.observed: On the top sheet, the NFC SDA label NET0017 runs to MCU pin 61 (PB8), and the NFC SCL label NET0001 runs to MCU pin 62 (PB9). The nfc_ic sheet labels U3.5 (SDA) as NET0017 and U3.3 (SCL) as NET0001, so the I2C lines appear swapped relative to the specification.
anomalies.expected: Specification: "NFC_SDA net: U2 pin 62 (PB9) — R1 (10 kΩ) to VCC — U3 pin 5 (SDA)" and "NFC_SCL net: U2 pin 61 (PB8) — R2 (10 kΩ) to VCC — U3 pin 3 (SCL)". On the STM32L476, PB8 is the I2C1_SCL alternate function and PB9 is I2C1_SDA, so SDA should be on PB9.

evidence.quote: NFC_SDA net: U2 pin 62 (`PB9`) — R1 (10 kΩ) to VCC — U3 pin 5 (`SDA`)
NFC_SCL net: U2 pin 61 (`PB8`) — R2 (10 kΩ) to VCC — U3 pin 3 (`SCL`)
PB8 61 / PB9 62 pins with labels NET0017 and NET0001 (Id 1/3, top sheet); nfc_ic sheet: SDA 5 → NET0017, SCL 3 → NET0001 (Id 2/3)

anomalies.impact: The NFC I2C bus has SDA and SCL on the wrong MCU pins. Hardware I2C1 would not function, and bit-banged firmware would need to be written against the swapped pins, so NFC communication would fail as designed.

anomalies.observed: The BS0 pin (pin 10) appears to be routed up to the VCC wire at the top of the display sheet, not to GND. The BS1/BS2 strapping near the GND symbol is hard to trace in the drawing, so this reading is uncertain.
anomalies.expected: Specification: "BS0 (pin 10) → GND, BS1 (pin 11) → VCC, BS2 (pin 12) → GND", which gives the I2C interface-select strapping 010.

evidence.quote: `BS0` (pin 10) → GND; `BS1` (pin 11) → VCC; `BS2` (pin 12) → GND. That BS2,BS1,BS0 = 0,1,0 strapping
display.kicad_sch (Id 3/3): BS0 10, BS1 11, BS2 12 pins with VCC arrow at top joining a horizontal wire at the top of the sheet

anomalies.impact: If BS0 is tied high, the SSD1306 may select a different interface mode (not I2C), so the OLED would not respond to the MCU's I2C traffic.

parsed.summary: The main anomaly is that the NFC I2C lines appear swapped: SDA (NET0017) goes to PB8 and SCL (NET0001) goes to PB9, which contradicts the specification and the STM32 I2C1 pin mapping. A second, lower-confidence possibility is a BS0 strap error on the OLED, which is hard to verify in the drawing.
